question: God spoke in time past by the prophets. By whom has He spoken to us in these last days?
explanation: The chapter says God has spoken to us by His Son.

question: What did the Son do after purging our sins?
choices: Sat down at the right hand of Majesty
explanation: When He had by Himself purged our sins, He sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high.

question: How does Hebrews 1 describe the Son in relation to God's glory?
explanation: The Son is called the brightness of God's glory and the express image of His person.

question: To what beings is the Son shown to be superior?
explanation: The chapter emphasizes Christ's superiority over angels.

question: What does God say to the Son that He never said to any of the angels?
choices: Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee
explanation: God says, 'Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee,' and the writer asks to which of the angels He ever said that.

question: What are believers warned not to let happen?
explanation: The writer warns them to give earnest heed so they do not drift from what they heard.

question: What question does the writer ask as a warning?
choices: Why did Israel fall in the wilderness?
Where shall we go for truth?
How shall we escape if we neglect so great salvation?
explanation: The chapter warns against neglecting the salvation announced by the Lord.

question: Why was Jesus made a little lower than the angels?
explanation: Jesus humbled Himself so He could suffer death for everyone.

question: What did Jesus destroy by His death?
choices: The one who had the power of death
explanation: Through death He destroyed him that had the power of death, that is, the devil.

question: What role does Jesus fulfill?
explanation: He became a merciful and faithful high priest to make reconciliation for sins.

question: Whom are believers told to consider?
choices: Jesus the Apostle and High Priest of our profession
explanation: The chapter calls believers to fix their attention on Jesus.

question: Jesus is counted worthy of more glory than whom?
explanation: Jesus is greater than Moses as the builder is greater than the house.

question: What warning from Israel's history is repeated?
explanation: The writer quotes Psalm 95 and warns against a hardened heart.

question: What kept the wilderness generation from entering God's rest?
explanation: They could not enter because of unbelief.

question: How is Moses described in God's house?
explanation: Moses was faithful as a servant, but Christ is over the house as a Son.

question: What promise still remains?
explanation: The chapter says the promise of entering His rest still stands.

question: Why did the word preached not profit some?
choices: It was not mixed with faith
explanation: The message did not benefit them because it was not received with faith.

question: How is the word of God described?
explanation: The word of God is quick, which means living, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword.

question: Who is called the great High Priest?
explanation: Believers are told to hold fast because Jesus is the great High Priest.

question: How are believers told to come to the throne of grace?
explanation: They are invited to come boldly to receive mercy and grace.

question: What is every high priest taken from among men ordained to do?
choices: Offer gifts and sacrifices for sins
explanation: The high priest represents people before God in matters concerning sin offerings.

question: What order is Jesus called a priest after?
explanation: Jesus is designated a high priest after the order of Melchizedek.

question: What did Jesus learn through the things He suffered?
explanation: Though He was a Son, He learned obedience through suffering.

question: What image is used for spiritually immature believers?
explanation: They still needed milk rather than strong meat.

question: Who is strong meat for?
explanation: Strong meat belongs to the mature, whose senses are trained.

question: What are believers urged to go on unto?
explanation: They are told to leave the elementary principles and go on to maturity.

question: What agricultural picture is used to contrast blessing and rejection?
choices: Rain on fruitful land and thorny ground
explanation: Land that drinks rain and bears useful fruit is blessed, but land bearing thorns is near cursing.

question: What did God use to confirm His promise to Abraham?
explanation: God swore by Himself because He could swear by no greater.

question: How is hope described?
explanation: Hope is called a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul.

question: Who entered within the veil as our forerunner?
explanation: Jesus entered before us as the forerunner and eternal high priest.

question: Who met Abraham as he returned from the slaughter of the kings?
explanation: Melchizedek met Abraham and blessed him.

question: What did Abraham give Melchizedek?
explanation: Abraham gave him tithes of all.

question: What does Hebrews 7 say Jesus is able to do because He continues forever?
explanation: Because He lives forever, He can save completely those who come to God through Him.

question: Why does Jesus have an unchangeable priesthood?
explanation: His priesthood does not pass to another because He remains forever.

question: What kind of high priest is Jesus described as?
explanation: Jesus is the sinless high priest perfectly suited for His people.

question: Where is our High Priest seated?
choices: At the right hand of the throne of Majesty in heaven
explanation: The main point is that Jesus ministers from heaven at God's right hand.

question: What does Hebrews 8 call the earthly tabernacle system compared with the heavenly one?
explanation: The earthly priests serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things.

question: What kind of covenant does Jesus mediate?
explanation: Jesus is mediator of a better covenant established upon better promises.

question: Where does God say He will put His laws in the new covenant?
explanation: God promises an inward writing of His law.

question: What does Hebrews 8:12 say God will remember no more?
explanation: Under the new covenant God promises full forgiveness.

question: How often did the high priest enter the holiest place under the old covenant?
explanation: The high priest entered alone once a year, not without blood.

question: By what did Christ enter the holy place?
explanation: Christ obtained eternal redemption through His own blood.

question: What does the blood of Christ purge?
explanation: His blood cleanses the conscience from dead works to serve the living God.

question: Which principle about forgiveness does the chapter state?
choices: Without shedding of blood is no remission
explanation: The chapter states that forgiveness requires shedding of blood.

question: How many times was Christ offered to bear the sins of many?
explanation: Christ was offered once and will appear again for salvation to those who look for Him.

question: What is the law called?
choices: A shadow of good things to come
explanation: The law is described as a shadow rather than the very image.

question: By how many offerings has Christ perfected forever those who are sanctified?
explanation: Jesus perfected forever by His single offering.

question: What new access do believers have?
explanation: Believers now have boldness to enter the holiest by Jesus' blood.

question: What are believers told not to forsake?
explanation: They are warned not to neglect meeting together.

question: What does Hebrews 10:31 say it is fearful to fall into?
choices: The hands of the living God
explanation: The chapter closes its warning with that solemn statement.

question: How does Hebrews 11:1 describe faith?
choices: The substance of things hoped for and evidence of things not seen
explanation: Faith is described as confidence in what is hoped for and conviction about what is unseen.

question: Who built an ark to the saving of his house?
explanation: Noah obeyed God in reverent faith and prepared the ark.

question: Who went out not knowing where he was going?
explanation: Abraham went out by faith when called to inherit a place.

question: What did Moses choose?
choices: To suffer affliction with the people of God
explanation: Moses chose God's people over temporary pleasures of sin.

question: Who is named for receiving the spies with peace?
explanation: Rahab is included among the examples of faith.

question: Whom are believers told to look unto?
explanation: They are to look unto Jesus, the author and finisher of faith.

question: What did Jesus endure?
explanation: For the joy set before Him, Jesus endured the cross and despised the shame.

question: Whom does the Lord chasten?
explanation: Discipline is presented as a sign of God's fatherly love.

question: What kind of fruit does chastening yield?
explanation: Though painful at first, discipline later produces righteous peace.

question: What kind of kingdom do believers receive?
choices: A kingdom which cannot be moved
explanation: The chapter ends by reminding believers they receive an unshakable kingdom.

question: What does Hebrews 13:1 say should continue?
explanation: The chapter begins with the command, 'Let brotherly love continue.'

question: What might some people have done by showing hospitality?
explanation: The writer reminds them that some have entertained angels without knowing it.

question: What does Hebrews 13:5 say believers should be without?
explanation: They are to be content and free from the love of money.

question: How is Jesus Christ described?
choices: The same yesterday, today, and forever
explanation: His unchanging character is emphasized.

question: What sacrifice are believers to offer continually to God?
explanation: Believers now offer praise, the fruit of lips giving thanks to His name.

question: By faith, Abel offered a more excellent sacrifice than whom?
explanation: By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain.

question: Who was translated that he should not see death?
explanation: By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death.

question: What is impossible without faith?
explanation: Without faith it is impossible to please him.

question: Who received strength to conceive seed when she was past age?
explanation: Through faith also Sara herself received strength to conceive seed, and was delivered of a child when she was past age.

question: Whom did Abraham offer up when he was tried?
explanation: By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac.

question: Whom did Isaac bless by faith concerning things to come?
explanation: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.

question: Whose two sons did Jacob bless when he was dying?
explanation: By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph.

question: What did Joseph, when he died, give commandment about?
explanation: By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel; and gave commandment concerning his bones.

question: For how long was Moses hid by his parents when he was born?
explanation: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents.

question: What did Moses refuse to be called when he came to years?
explanation: By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter.

question: Who, though dead, yet speaketh?
explanation: By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice, and by it he being dead yet speaketh.

question: What must he that cometh to God believe about God?
choices: That he is, and a rewarder of them that diligently seek him
That he is just and slow to anger
That he is a king over all nations
That he forgives all who ask
explanation: He that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.

question: What did Noah do to the world by preparing the ark?
explanation: Noah prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world.

question: In what did Abraham dwell in the land of promise with Isaac and Jacob?
explanation: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob.

question: What city did Abraham look for?
choices: One with foundations, whose builder and maker is God
explanation: He looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.

question: Why did Sara receive strength to conceive?
choices: She judged him faithful who had promised
explanation: Sara received strength to conceive seed... because she judged him faithful who had promised.

question: To what is the multitude from one man as good as dead compared?
choices: The stars of the sky and the sand by the sea shore
The drops of the morning dew
explanation: Therefore sprang there even of one, and him as good as dead, so many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable.

question: What did those who died in faith confess they were on the earth?
explanation: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.

question: What did Abraham account that God was able to do for Isaac?
choices: Raise him up, even from the dead
explanation: Accounting that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead.

question: What had God said about Isaac before Abraham offered him?
choices: Isaac shall be a great nation
In Isaac shall thy seed be called
explanation: Of whom it was said, That in Isaac shall thy seed be called.

question: What was Jacob doing as he blessed Joseph's sons and worshipped?
choices: Leaning upon the top of his staff
explanation: Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.

question: Why did Moses' parents hide him for three months?
choices: They saw he was a proper child
explanation: They saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king's commandment.

question: What did Moses esteem greater riches than the treasures in Egypt?
explanation: Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt.

question: Why did Moses keep the passover and the sprinkling of blood?
choices: Lest he that destroyed the firstborn should touch them
To end the plagues of frogs
explanation: Through faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he that destroyed the firstborn should touch them.

question: What fell down by faith after the people compassed it seven days?
explanation: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they were compassed about seven days.

question: What testimony did Enoch have before his translation?
choices: That he walked with the Lord
explanation: Before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.

question: Of what did Noah become heir?
choices: The righteousness which is by faith
explanation: Noah became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.

question: What opportunity does the text say those who died in faith might have had if mindful of their old country?
explanation: If they had been mindful of that country from whence they came out, they might have had opportunity to have returned.

question: Why is God not ashamed to be called their God?
choices: He hath prepared for them a city
explanation: God is not ashamed to be called their God: for he hath prepared for them a city.

question: What did Joseph make mention of when he died?
choices: The departing of the children of Israel
explanation: Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel.

question: Of what were Moses' parents not afraid?
explanation: They saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king's commandment.

question: How did Moses endure when he forsook Egypt?
choices: With the staff in his hand
As seeing him who is invisible
explanation: By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.

question: What happened to the Egyptians when they tried to cross the Red sea as by dry land?
explanation: By faith they passed through the Red sea as by dry land: which the Egyptians assaying to do were drowned.

question: Which of these is NOT named among those the writer lacks time to tell of?
explanation: The writer names Gedeon, Barak, Samson, Jephthae, David, Samuel and the prophets; Joshua is not among them.

question: What did those who acted through faith stop?
explanation: Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions.

question: What did those through faith quench?
explanation: Through faith they quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword.

question: What did women receive through faith?
choices: Their dead raised to life again
explanation: Women received their dead raised to life again.

question: What did some wander about in, being destitute and afflicted?
explanation: They wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented.

question: By what were the worlds framed?
explanation: Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God.

question: What did God provide so that those of old should not be made perfect without us?
explanation: God having provided some better thing for us, that they without us should not be made perfect.

question: What are believers compassed about with?
explanation: Seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us run with patience the race that is set before us.

question: What are we told to lay aside as we run the race?
choices: Every weight and the sin that easily besets us
explanation: Let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us.

question: Who is called the author and finisher of our faith?
explanation: Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith.

question: Where is Jesus now set down?
choices: At the right hand of the throne of God
At the table of the firstborn
explanation: Jesus is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.

question: Who sold his birthright for one morsel of meat?
explanation: Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.

question: To which mount have believers come, according to the writer?
explanation: But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem.

question: Jesus is the mediator of what?
explanation: And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling.

question: What does the writer say our God is?
explanation: For our God is a consuming fire.

question: What are we told to follow with all men, along with holiness?
explanation: Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord.

question: Who said, "I exceedingly fear and quake" at the mountain?
explanation: So terrible was the sight, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake.

question: How are we told to run the race that is set before us?
explanation: Let us run with patience the race that is set before us.

question: What did Jesus do to the shame as he endured the cross?
explanation: Jesus, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame.

question: How far had the readers resisted in striving against sin?
explanation: Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin.

question: What are believers told not to despise?
explanation: My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him.

question: What are those called who are without chastisement?
explanation: If ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.

question: Whom do we give reverence to, and to whom should we much rather be in subjection?
choices: Fathers of our flesh; the Father of spirits
explanation: We have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?

question: Why does God chasten us?
choices: For our profit, that we may be partakers of his holiness
explanation: He chastens us for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness.

question: How does no chastening seem for the present?
explanation: No chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous.

question: What are we told to lift up?
choices: The hands which hang down, and the feeble knees
explanation: Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees.

question: What does a root of bitterness springing up do?
explanation: Lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled.

question: What did Esau find no place of, though he sought it carefully with tears?
explanation: He was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.

question: What was said would happen to a beast that touched the mountain?
choices: It would be stoned or thrust through with a dart
explanation: If so much as a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned, or thrust through with a dart.

question: What do believers come to along with the heavenly Jerusalem?
explanation: Ye are come unto the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels.

question: What speaks better things than the blood of Abel?
explanation: To the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel.

question: What did the mount that might be touched do?
explanation: Ye are not come unto the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire.

question: What does the writer say believers should consider, lest they be wearied and faint?
choices: Him that endured such contradiction of sinners
explanation: Consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds.

question: As what does the exhortation about chastening speak to believers?
explanation: Ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children.

question: How long did earthly fathers chasten us, and by whose pleasure?
choices: A few days, after their own pleasure
A season, after the Lord's will
explanation: They verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit.

question: What does the writer say to make for your feet, lest the lame be turned out of the way?
explanation: Make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed.

question: Without what shall no man see the Lord?
explanation: Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord.

question: Which three things surrounded the mount that burned with fire?
explanation: Ye are not come unto the mount that burned with fire, nor unto blackness, and darkness, and tempest.

question: What did those who heard the voice entreat?
choices: That Moses should speak for them
That the fire be put out
That the word should not be spoken to them any more
explanation: The voice of words; which voice they that heard intreated that the word should not be spoken to them any more.

question: Whose names are written in heaven, in the general assembly?
explanation: To the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven.

question: Who is God called when believers come to him in Mount Sion?
explanation: And to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect.

question: What has the Lord promised to shake besides the earth?
explanation: Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.

question: What does the word "Yet once more" signify?
choices: The removing of things that are shaken
explanation: This word, Yet once more, signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken, that those things which cannot be shaken may remain.

question: How are believers to serve God acceptably?
explanation: Let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear.

question: What happens to us if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven?
choices: The law will stand for us
We shall not escape, much more than they
explanation: If they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth, much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven.

question: What could those at the mountain not endure?
explanation: For they could not endure that which was commanded, And if so much as a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned.

question: Looking diligently, what are believers told to take care no man fails of?
explanation: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God.

question: Whom are believers told to remember as though bound with them?
explanation: Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them.

question: What does the writer say is honourable in all?
explanation: Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled.

question: What has God said to those who are content?
choices: I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee
explanation: Be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.

question: What can believers boldly say about the Lord?
explanation: We may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me.

question: Where did Jesus suffer, to sanctify the people with his own blood?
explanation: Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate.

question: What do believers have no continuing here?
explanation: For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come.

question: What two things are we told not to forget, with which God is well pleased?
choices: To do good and to communicate
explanation: But to do good and to communicate forget not: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.

question: Who is set at liberty, according to the writer?
explanation: Know ye that our brother Timothy is set at liberty.

question: What is Jesus called, brought again from the dead?
choices: That great shepherd of the sheep
explanation: The God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep.

question: Who send their greetings at the end of the letter?
explanation: They of Italy salute you.

question: Whom will God judge?
explanation: Whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.

question: What should your conversation be without, and with what should you be content?
choices: Covetousness; such things as ye have
explanation: Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have.

question: Whom are believers told to remember, and whose faith to follow?
choices: Them which have the rule over you, who spoke the word of God
explanation: Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow.

question: What should the heart be established with, not meats?
explanation: It is a good thing that the heart be established with grace; not with meats.

question: Where were the bodies of the beasts burned whose blood was brought into the sanctuary?
choices: At the gate of the temple
explanation: The bodies of those beasts, whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin, are burned without the camp.

question: With what did Jesus sanctify the people?
explanation: Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate.

question: What are believers told to bear as they go forth unto him without the camp?
explanation: Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach.

question: What is the sacrifice of praise, according to the writer?
choices: The fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name
explanation: The sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name.

question: Why are believers told to obey them that have the rule over them?
choices: They watch for your souls, as they that must give account
They are the elders of Israel
explanation: Obey them that have the rule over you: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account.

question: What does the writer say he and his companions trust they have?
explanation: Pray for us: for we trust we have a good conscience, in all things willing to live honestly.

question: Through what blood did God bring again our Lord Jesus from the dead?
explanation: The God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, through the blood of the everlasting covenant.

question: What does the writer ask God to make you perfect in?
choices: Every good work to do his will
explanation: Make you perfect in every good work to do his will, working in you that which is wellpleasing in his sight.

question: How does the writer say he has written his letter?
explanation: Suffer the word of exhortation: for I have written a letter unto you in few words.

question: What do some, who entertain strangers, thereby entertain?
explanation: Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.

question: Why are we told to remember those who suffer adversity?
choices: We are ourselves also in the body
They are our brothers in the temple
explanation: Remember them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body.

question: What does the writer say to consider about those who had the rule?
explanation: Whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation.

question: What have meats done for those occupied with them?
explanation: Be not carried about with divers and strange doctrines... not with meats, which have not profited them that have been occupied therein.

question: Who has no right to eat of the altar the writer speaks of?
explanation: We have an altar, whereof they have no right to eat which serve the tabernacle.

question: Why does the writer want those who rule to do it with joy, not grief?
explanation: That they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you.

question: Why does the writer beseech them to pray for him?
choices: That he may be restored to them the sooner
That he may be freed from prison
explanation: But I beseech you the rather to do this, that I may be restored to you the sooner.

question: What does the writer say he will do if Timothy comes shortly?
explanation: Timothy is set at liberty; with whom, if he come shortly, I will see you.

question: Whom are the readers told to salute, besides the saints?
choices: All them that have the rule over you
explanation: Salute all them that have the rule over you, and all the saints.

question: Who brings the blood of the beasts into the sanctuary for sin?
explanation: The bodies of those beasts, whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin, are burned without the camp.

question: What does God work in you through Jesus Christ?
choices: That which is wellpleasing in his sight
explanation: Working in you that which is wellpleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ.

question: What does the writer say is undefiled, along with marriage being honourable?
explanation: Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled.

question: What are all the angels of God told to do to the firstbegotten?
explanation: God says, "Let all the angels of God worship him."

question: What has God appointed his Son to be heir of?
explanation: God hath appointed his Son heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds.

question: What does the Son uphold all things by?
explanation: The Son is upholding all things by the word of his power.

question: What has the Son obtained by inheritance that is more excellent than the angels have?
explanation: He hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than the angels.

question: What does God make his ministers, in what is said of the angels?
explanation: Of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.

question: What is said of the Son's throne?
choices: It is for ever and ever
It stands until the last day
It stands until his enemies are put down
explanation: Unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever.

question: Why has God anointed the Son with the oil of gladness above his fellows?
choices: He was born of the fathers
He loved righteousness and hated iniquity
explanation: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

question: What are the heavens called in the words spoken to the Lord?
explanation: Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of thine hands.

question: Why are the angels sent forth to minister?
choices: For them who shall be heirs of salvation
To carry the prophets to the fathers
To guard the throne of the Majesty
explanation: They are all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation.

question: The heavens and the earth shall wax old as doth what?
explanation: They all shall wax old as doth a garment.

question: What will the Son do to the heavens, as a vesture?
explanation: As a vesture shalt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed.

question: What will God make of the Son's enemies?
explanation: Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.

question: The Son is called the express image of what?
explanation: The Son is the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person.

question: To whom did God speak in time past by the prophets?
explanation: God spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets.

question: What is the sceptre of the Son's kingdom called?
explanation: A sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom.

question: While the heavens perish, what is said of the Son?
explanation: They shall be changed: but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail.

question: The Son took on him the seed of whom?
explanation: He took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham.

question: What did Jesus taste for every man?
explanation: Jesus was made a little lower than the angels that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.

question: Why is Jesus able to help those who are tempted?
choices: He is higher than the angels
He sat down on the right hand
explanation: In that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted.

question: What does Jesus call those he sanctifies?
explanation: He is not ashamed to call them brethren.

question: What did every transgression and disobedience receive under the word spoken by angels?
explanation: The word spoken by angels was stedfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompence of reward.

question: Who first began to speak the great salvation?
explanation: It at the first began to be spoken by the Lord.

question: By whom was the salvation confirmed unto us?
explanation: It was confirmed unto us by them that heard him.

question: What did God bear witness with, along with signs and wonders?
choices: Divers miracles and gifts of the Holy Ghost
explanation: God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost.

question: What did God set man over, in the words quoted from the Psalm?
explanation: Thou crownedst him with glory and honour, and didst set him over the works of thy hands.

question: Through fear of what were people all their lifetime subject to bondage?
explanation: Jesus delivers them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.

question: How was the captain of their salvation made perfect?
explanation: It became God to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.

question: What does the Son say he will do in the midst of the church?
explanation: In the midst of the church will I sing praise unto thee.

question: What do we not yet see?
explanation: Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet... But now we see not yet all things put under him.

question: The words quoted from the Psalm ask what is man that thou visitest whom?
explanation: What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him?

question: What is man crowned with, in the quoted words?
explanation: Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; thou crownedst him with glory and honour.

question: What does the Son say he will put in God?
explanation: And again, I will put my trust in him.

question: To whom did God not put the world to come in subjection?
explanation: Unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come, whereof we speak.

question: To whom did it behove Jesus to be made like in all things?
explanation: In all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren.

question: What does the Son say he will declare unto his brethren?
explanation: I will declare thy name unto my brethren.

question: Of what are the children partakers?
explanation: The children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same.

question: Jesus was made a merciful and faithful high priest to make what for the sins of the people?
explanation: He was made like his brethren to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.

question: Who has given the children to the Son?
explanation: Behold I and the children which God hath given me.

question: Who was faithful to him that appointed him, as Moses was faithful in all his house?
explanation: Christ Jesus was faithful to him that appointed him, as also Moses was faithful in all his house.

question: For how long did the fathers see God's works in the wilderness?
explanation: Your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works forty years.

question: Where did the carcases of those who sinned fall?
explanation: God was grieved with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness.

question: Who led the people out of Egypt in this chapter?
explanation: Not all that came out of Egypt by Moses provoked God.

question: Whose house are we, if we hold fast the confidence and rejoicing of the hope?
explanation: Christ is a son over his own house; whose house are we, if we hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm unto the end.

question: Who built all things?
explanation: Every house is builded by some man; but he that built all things is God.

question: Why was Christ counted worthy of more glory than Moses?
choices: He led more people out of Egypt
He who built the house has more honour than the house
He was born in a greater house
explanation: He who hath builded the house hath more honour than the house.

question: What is Christ over his own house?
explanation: Moses was faithful as a servant, but Christ as a son over his own house.

question: What did God say they do alway err in?
explanation: They do alway err in their heart; and they have not known my ways.

question: What did God swear in his wrath?
choices: They shall not enter into my rest
They shall not see the land of Egypt
explanation: So I sware in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.

question: What kind of heart are the brethren warned against, departing from the living God?
explanation: Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God.

question: How often are the brethren to exhort one another?
explanation: Exhort one another daily, while it is called To day.

question: What may harden any of you if you do not exhort one another?
explanation: Exhort one another daily; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.

question: With whom was God grieved forty years?
explanation: But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned?

question: To whom did God swear that they should not enter into his rest?
explanation: To whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not?

question: Of whom are we made partakers, if we hold our confidence stedfast unto the end?
explanation: We are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end.

question: Moses was faithful as a servant for a testimony of what?
choices: Those things which were to be spoken after
explanation: Moses was faithful as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were to be spoken after.

question: Of what calling are the holy brethren partakers?
explanation: Holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest.

question: In the day of what, in the wilderness, were hearts hardened?
explanation: Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness.

question: What did the fathers see while they tempted and proved God?
explanation: Your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works forty years.

question: What did some who heard do, though not all who came out of Egypt did it?
explanation: For some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses.

question: What did God say of that generation, besides that they err in their heart?
choices: They have not known my ways
They have not kept my name
They have not heard my law
They have not seen my glory
explanation: They do alway err in their heart; and they have not known my ways.

question: By whom is every house built?
explanation: For every house is builded by some man; but he that built all things is God.

question: From whom is the evil heart of unbelief departing?
explanation: An evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God.

question: What must we hold fast firm unto the end?
choices: The confidence and the rejoicing of the hope
explanation: Hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm unto the end.

question: On which day did God rest from all his works?
explanation: God did rest the seventh day from all his works.

question: What is the word of God sharper than?
explanation: The word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword.

question: How was our high priest tempted?
choices: In all points like as we are
explanation: He was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.

question: What is the word of God a discerner of?
choices: The thoughts and intents of the heart
explanation: The word of God is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.

question: Through whom did God limit a certain day, saying "To day"?
explanation: He limiteth a certain day, saying in David, To day, after so long a time.

question: What do we who have believed do?
explanation: We which have believed do enter into rest.

question: What may we obtain and find at the throne of grace?
choices: Mercy and grace to help in time of need
explanation: Let us come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.

question: What is true of all things in his sight?
choices: They are written in a book
explanation: All things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.

question: We have not a high priest who cannot be touched with the feeling of what?
explanation: We have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities.

question: What has he done who is entered into his rest?
explanation: He that is entered into his rest hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.

question: What are we told to labour to do?
explanation: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.

question: If Jesus had given them rest, what would not have been spoken afterward?
explanation: If Jesus had given them rest, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day.

question: Since when were God's works finished?
explanation: The works were finished from the foundation of the world.

question: To whom remaineth a rest?
explanation: There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.

question: What did God swear in his wrath about those who did not believe?
choices: They should not enter into his rest
They should not see the land
They should die in the wilderness
explanation: As I have sworn in my wrath, if they shall enter into my rest.

question: What example are we warned not to fall after?
explanation: Lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.

question: What are we told to hold fast, since we have a great high priest?
explanation: Seeing then that we have a great high priest, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.

question: What are we told to fear, since a promise of entering his rest is left us?
choices: That any should come short of it
That the law should be lost
That the day should not come
explanation: Let us therefore fear, lest any of you should seem to come short of it.

question: Where has our great high priest passed into?
explanation: We have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God.

question: Who was called of God as a high priest, in this chapter?
explanation: No man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron.

question: What did Jesus offer up with strong crying and tears?
explanation: In the days of his flesh he offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears.

question: Why can a high priest have compassion on the ignorant?
choices: He himself is compassed with infirmity
He is taken from the angels
explanation: He can have compassion because he himself also is compassed with infirmity.

question: For whom must the high priest offer for sins, besides the people?
explanation: By reason hereof he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.

question: Who did not glorify himself to be made a high priest?
explanation: Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest; but he that said unto him, Thou art my Son.

question: He that useth milk is unskilful in what?
explanation: Every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.

question: What did they need to be taught again, when they ought to be teachers?
choices: The first principles of the oracles of God
explanation: Ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God.

question: What did Jesus become, once made perfect, to all that obey him?
explanation: Being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him.

question: Why are many things hard to be uttered about Melchisedec?
explanation: Of whom we have many things to say, and hard to be uttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing.

question: How long is Christ a priest, in the words from another place?
explanation: Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.

question: What do those of full age discern by use of their senses?
explanation: Their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.

question: In what was Jesus heard, when he prayed to him that was able to save him from death?
explanation: He offered up prayers... unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared.

question: What ought the readers already to be, by reason of the time?
explanation: For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again.

question: To whom is Christ the author of eternal salvation?
choices: All who are of full age
explanation: He became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him.

question: On whom can the high priest have compassion?
choices: The ignorant and them that are out of the way
explanation: Who can have compassion on the ignorant, and on them that are out of the way.

question: In things pertaining to whom is every high priest ordained for men?
explanation: Every high priest taken from among men is ordained for men in things pertaining to God.
